Method of Attack: Encrypts data using AES-256 encryption and appends .crjoker extension to targeted files
Scans all drives including mapped network drives for files with targeted extensions
Sends victim information (date, hostname, username, machine name) to Command & Control server
Terminates Regedit and Taskmgr processes to prevent interference
Creates batch file to delete Shadow Volume Copies and disable Windows automatic startup repair
Displays ransom note window demanding ransom in bitcoins via email communication
Attack Vector: Disguised installer as PDF file, likely distributed via email phishing campaigns
Indicators of Compromise: Email addresses for ransom communication: file987@sigaint.org, file9876@openmail.cc, file987@tutanota.com
Files in %Temp% folder: crjoker.html, drvpci.exe, GetYouFiles.txt, imgdesktop.exe, new.bat, README!!!.txt, sdajfhdfkj, windefrag.exe, windrv.exe, winpnp.exe
Registry entries under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run for winpnp, drvpci, windefrag executables
Batch file commands: vssadmin.exe Delete Shadows /All /Quiet, bcdedit.exe /set {default} recoveryenabled No, bcdedit.exe /set {default} bootstatuspolicy ignoreallfailures
